cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A consensus algorithm lets a group of nodes agree on one value, or one ordered log, such as who the leader is or whether a write committed, even when some nodes crash or messages are lost. Paxos and Raft are the two main ones.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Both use majority quorums: a write commits once a majority (floor of N/2 plus 1) accepts it, and any two majorities overlap, so committed values are never lost. Raft elects a leader per term with randomized timeouts and replicates its log. Quorum also prevents split-brain. etcd and ZooKeeper use this.

questions.q: Is a 4-node cluster more fault-tolerant than 3?
questions.a: No. It needs a majority of 3 and still tolerates only 1 failure, while adding a machine that must acknowledge writes.
Only the side of a partition with a majority can commit writes, so two sides cannot diverge.
To be understandable, giving Multi-Paxos guarantees split into leader election, log replication and safety.
